pairs.difference: A: orange and yellow towel stripes on a green checker. It is a clean near-complementary pair, and the fold shadows drift slightly rose. The background sits at the top of the real range (0.217). B: navy calculator on amber, with a muted grey LCD and dull red panel that give neutral rest and one cyan accent. All fields on both cards are inside the real ranges, and neither shows the cream-neutral or hot-orange drift from the lessons.

A: copper lamp on chartreuse rays. The pale cool-grey glass chimney gives a real neutral rest. B: wax, flames and brass candelabra all share one warm peach-gold, and the lens merges wax and metal into a single salmon mass on purple. There is no cool or neutral on the subject, like the cream drift on the generated computers. The evidence is thin because both are in range.
pairs.fix: Make the wax candles a cooler off-white with pale grey-lilac shading, and make the brass a darker, duller yellow-brown so wax and metal read as two different colors.

pairs.difference: A: pumpkin orange and floor orange are the same loud hue on a loud violet wall. Subject 0.182 and background 0.196 are both above the real ranges, so nothing rests the eye and the card is effectively orange plus purple (3.04 families). B: yellow duck with red and blue accents, a muted sand floor and a darker green wall. Its subject is only just over the range (0.165), and the sand and pebbles give neutral relief.
pairs.fix: Make the wooden floor a dull grey-brown, not orange, and deepen the purple wall to a quieter tone. Make the pumpkin a slightly duller, natural orange with brown-green shading in the ribs.

pairs.difference: A: beige stone fountain with neon cyan water on warm brick. The stone is creamy and warm share is slightly high, but its shadow chroma (0.89) is normal. B: the cat body is nearly chromeless plum-black. Subject 0.047 and shadow kept 0.443 are both below the real ranges, and the lens shows brown-plum rims rather than the blue-grey body of the real camera on yellow. The saturated pink ears and red collar sit on this dead mass.
pairs.fix: Paint the black fur as deep blue-grey with visible cool blue light on the head and back, and let the shadows keep a navy color instead of going brown-black.

pairs.difference: A: navy cap with gold trim on cyan, a clear hue role with one warm accent, and rich blue shadows. B: the hat is a dull brownish plum with lighter dusty mauve on the crown, under a very saturated violet band, against hot orange rings. Warm share (0.828) is over the range and the card leans warm. The hat's own color looks muddied by the orange. The margin is small.
pairs.fix: Make the hat a cleaner deep violet, with cool blue-purple light on the crown and no brown in it. Calm the orange rings toward yellow-orange.

pairs.difference: A is the lighthouse from the real reference cards: crimson red, grey-white stone and cool grey-blue cloud shadow. B: purple roof, mauve-pink stone, amber windows, yellow moon and green hill all compete at similar strength. The lens turns the clouds cream-green and the stone maroon, matching the yellowed clouds on the generated lighthouses. All neutrals in B are warm or pink.
pairs.fix: Make the clouds pure white with cool blue-grey shading, and make the stone a plain neutral grey. Keep purple only on the roof and quiet the moon to a pale cream.

pairs.difference: A: navy pot on pink stripes with lime slime and an orange flame. That is several loud accents, but the grey stone floor is a true neutral rest. B: gloves are one scarlet, and subject 0.182 is above the real range. The highlights swing to orange-tan in the lens, and shadows stay in red-maroon on an orange floor. This is the orange-leaning red seen on the generated lighthouses. The call is close because A's lime and pink are also loud.
pairs.fix: Use a deeper crimson red leather with soft pale pink-white highlights rather than orange ones. Shade toward dark wine, and make the floor wood duller and browner.

pairs.difference: A is the lion from the real reference cards: pale neutral marble, with only faint warm-green tint, set against varied natural greens. B: yellow bag on violet. Background 0.223 is far above the real range (0.086 to 0.147), so hero and background are equally loud. Bag yellow and handle orange are close to pure hue, with little neutral beyond the cream bottle.
pairs.fix: Lower the purple wall to a soft, slightly greyed lavender and make the bag a duller mustard canvas with brown-ochre folds.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is pure red in light and shadow, with subject 0.2165 above the real range and a gold-orange badge added. Against saturated cyan the card has no resting color and the red has no local variation. B: broom with yellow straw, red-brown handle and a small red binding. Chroma (0.146) is in range, and the lens reads it as one muted brown mass against the blue.
pairs.fix: Make the scarf a slightly deeper cotton red with darker wine folds and a softer, paler highlight. Tone the badge gold down to a dull brass.

pairs.difference: A: brown coffin whose shadows lose color (shadow kept 0.588 is below the real range, and background 0.153 is slightly above). The side falls to dead dark brown against bright yellow-green grass and pure cyan sky, with a yellow cross and a purple lining in addition. B: lilac-grey stone with cool shading and navy and cream squares, in the cool-neutral direction of the real cards. Its chroma and family count are low, but the cool shadow on the stone looks deliberate.
pairs.fix: Shade the coffin's side with deep red-brown and a hint of plum so it stays colorful, make the grass a duller, darker green, and soften the sky.

pairs.difference: A: blue sphere with lavender cloud, gold stand, brown wood and a medium green diamond wall. Background 0.169 is in range and the wood gives a quiet base. B: neon violet wall at 0.24, above the real range, with orange drink, pink straw and a cyan parasol all near pure hue. Shadow chroma is at the top (1.449). The hero and wall are equally loud with no neutral rest.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a soft dusty lavender, the straw a plain muted red, and the parasol a pale aqua. Let the glass rim and ice stay colorless grey-white.

pairs.difference: A: blue sneakers with lime, teal, magenta and orange details. Five-plus families are above the range, and the background is soft, slightly muted orange and cream. B: the grey headstone has very low chroma (0.031) and warm share is 0.916 above the range. The lens shows the stone as tan and mauve, not cool grey, on a flat single orange wall with a cream floor. The warm cast takes over the neutral, matching the lesson computers, but A is also suspiciously confetti-like.
pairs.fix: Make the headstone a clear cool blue-grey in shadow and a light neutral grey on top, and add a soft lighter glow to the orange wall behind it.

pattern: Generated cards are given away by color casts and hue discipline, not by being simply brighter. Neutrals drift warm: whites, stone, wax and clouds turn cream or tan, where real cards keep grey-white with cool blue-lilac shade (computer side, lighthouse clouds). Reds and oranges lean hot, with orange highlights and scarlet in place of crimson, and shadows stay in the same hue or go dead brown instead of shifting to a related cool plum or navy. Hero and background are often equally loud, with little muted mass to rest the eye. Caveats: the metrics are weak on single fields, since real cards can also be low chroma, and p01 gave no color reason to choose. p06 and p08 lean partly on A being recognised as a labelled real reference. The 'horror' in the file path and the card subjects were deliberately not used as evidence; these calls rest on color only.
